question: How does each of the five define and report advisor headcount -- and what does each definition include or exclude?

claims.text: Definition - Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management supplement for the quarter ended December 31, 2020 (published 2021-01-20) labels its advisor headcount line "Wealth Management representatives", shown inside the advisor-led channel, at 15,950. The chunk gives no definition of who counts as a representative, and no more recent supplement in the evidence shows this line.

Definition - Edward Jones: The 10-Q for the period ended 2025-09-26 (published 2025-11-07) reports "Financial advisors (actual)". It defines Attrition % as "the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end." That defines attrition against the period-end count. It does not define who qualifies as a financial advisor.

Definition - Merrill: Merrill's advisor recruiting page (page content as of 2026-11-03) describes "Merrill Core Advisor (FA)" as the role reached "upon progression", once the Advisor Development Program is completed. Earlier roles are ADP Client Associate, ADP Financial Solutions Advisor and ADP Financial Advisor. This is a role description on a recruiting page, not a headcount definition from a financial filing.

Definition - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (period 2025-09-30, published 2025-11-25) states the firm "had 8,943 employee and independent contractor financial advisors affiliated with us as of September 30, 2025." It also states that "Advisors in our RCS division are not included in our financial advisor metric although their client assets are included in PCG AUA."

Includes - Schwab: Schwab's investor-day deck (published 2026-05-14) describes Schwab Advisor Network advisors as "independent and ... not employees or agents of Charles Schwab & Co., Inc." It says Schwab prescreens them and that they pay referral fees. The chunk does not say whether these advisors, or independent RIAs generally, are counted in any Schwab advisor total.

Includes - Edward Jones: The FY2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) reports financial advisors "(actual)" at year end. The count was 20,425 at year-end 2025, 20,125 at year-end 2024 and 19,232 at year-end 2023. The 10-K notes that "many of the Partnership's financial advisors are employees". The 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) says the firm operates in the U.S. and Canada, with "more than 20,000 financial advisors". The evidence does not say whether Associate Financial Advisors or trainees are counted.

Includes - Merrill: Merrill's recruiting page (page content as of 2026-11-03) describes a trainee path to Financial Advisor. It includes Advisor Development Program roles (ADP Client Associate, ADP Financial Solutions Advisor and ADP Financial Advisor, the last described as taking "Approximately 1-4 years") before Merrill Core Advisor. On the 2Q25 call (published 2025-07-16) the Bank of America CFO said the firm "continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through our extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors." Neither source says whether trainees are in a reported advisor count.

Includes - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) breaks the 8,943 total advisors at 2025-09-30 into 3,878 employees and 5,065 independent contractors. Raymond James says independent contractor advisors may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in its Financial Institutions Division. Management attributed the year's increase to "new recruits and trainees that were moved into production roles" exceeding departures and planned retirements.

Excludes - Edward Jones: The 10-Q for the period ended 2026-06-26 (published 2026-08-07) reports financial advisors (20,514 at period end) on a separate line from client support team professionals (20,654) and home office associates (8,808). The two support lines carry the footnote "Counted on a full-time equivalent basis". The financial advisor line is labelled "(actual)". The evidence does not say how part-time or retired advisors are treated.

Excludes - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) states that advisors in the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division "are not included in our financial advisor metric", although their client assets are in PCG AUA. Separately, the 10-K cites "approximately 19,500 associates (including 3,878 employee financial advisors) and 5,065 independent advisors". It describes associates as including "our employee financial advisors and all of our other employees", so non-advisor employees sit outside the 8,943 advisor metric.

Reporting - Morgan Stanley: The quarterly Wealth Management supplement for the quarter ended 2020-12-31 (published 2021-01-20) reports "Wealth Management representatives" at period end: 15,950 at Dec 31, 2020, 15,469 at Sep 30, 2020 and 15,468 at Dec 31, 2019. It shows them in the advisor-led channel, with percentage change columns.

Reporting - Schwab: On the 3Q26 earnings call (published 2026-10-15), the CEO described the advisor business by firms rather than advisors: "we serve more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets". Earlier calls and filings mention hiring "financial consultants and wealth advisers" and headcount growth that includes them (2Q26 10-Q, published 2026-08-07). The evidence shows no reported count of those advisors.

Reporting - Edward Jones: The FY2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) reports financial advisors at year end and on average: year-end 20,425 (2025), 20,125 (2024) and 19,232 (2023); average 20,331, 19,650 and 18,945. The 10-Q for the period ended 2026-06-26 (published 2026-08-07) reports period-end 20,514 and average 20,537, and in the MD&A tables gives two column sets, one of which reads 19,647 at period end. The 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) states "Financial advisor attrition was 6.1%", with a rise in departures among advisors with tenure of five years or less.

Reporting - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) has a table of financial advisors as of September 30 by channel. 2025: employees 3,878, independent contractors 5,065, total 8,943. 2024: 3,826, 4,961 and 8,787. 2023: 3,693, 5,019 and 8,712. On the 4Q25 call (published 2025-10-22), the CEO cited "a record number of financial advisors of 8,943". Recruiting is reported through trailing-12-month production and client assets at previous firms. On the 3Q FY26 call (published 2026-07-22), the CEO cited $156 million of production and nearly $23 billion of client assets for the quarter's recruits into the domestic independent contractor and employee channels. Management cites "departures and planned retirements" but gives no attrition rate in the evidence. Raymond James's Bank and Credit Union Advisors page (page content as of 2026-05-17) cites 940 advisors across 160 financial institutions.

adjacent.text: Bank of America's GWIM supplement for 4Q23 (published 2024-01-12) reports "Total wealth advisors" at period end: 18,916 at 12/31/2023 and 19,273 at 12/31/2022. Footnote 3 reads "Includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking."
adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's.

adjacent.text: Bank of America's November 2025 investor-day deck (segment GWIM) shows ">15K Wealth Advisors" for the Merrill | Private Bank combination.
adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley's 3Q26 supplement (published 2026-10-14) defines "Advisor-led client assets" as "client assets in accounts that have a Wealth Management representative assigned".
adjacent.differs_because: It defines a client-asset category, not the count of financial advisors or who is counted in it.

adjacent.text: Schwab's FY2025 10-K glossary (published 2026-02-25) defines "Assets receiving ongoing advisory services" as client assets custodied at the company "under the guidance of an independent advisor or enrolled in one of Schwab's managed investing solutions".
adjacent.differs_because: It defines an asset measure, not a count or definition of advisors.

adjacent.text: Schwab's 3Q26 press release (published 2026-10-15) reports full-time equivalent employees at quarter end of 33.9 thousand.
adjacent.differs_because: It counts all employees on a full-time-equivalent basis, not financial consultants, wealth advisors or independent RIAs.

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley - definition: no definition of 'financial advisor' or 'Wealth Management representative' headcount found in the evidence provided; only the 2020 label and the advisor-led client assets definition.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management financial supplement (definitions of performance metrics and terms) and the Form 10-K Wealth Management section

gaps.what: Schwab - definition: not found in the evidence provided. No Schwab disclosure defines 'financial advisor' or advisor headcount.
gaps.suggested_source: Schwab 10-K Item 1 and Item 7 glossary; Schwab investor-day materials on financial consultants and wealth advisors

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley - includes: not found in the evidence provided (trainees, employee vs. other, producing advisors).
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley financial supplement end notes and 10-K Wealth Management metrics

gaps.what: Edward Jones - includes: whether Associate Financial Advisors or trainee advisors are in the 'Financial advisors (actual)' count is not stated in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Edward Jones 10-K Item 1 and MD&A related-metrics footnotes

gaps.what: Merrill - includes: not found in the evidence provided. No Merrill-specific advisor count definition or inclusion rule (e.g., whether ADP trainees are counted) was found.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America GWIM supplement footnotes and 10-K GWIM section; Merrill advisor disclosures

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley - excludes: not found in the evidence provided (support staff, associates, part-time, retired, non-advisor roles).
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley financial supplement end notes and 10-K Wealth Management metrics

gaps.what: Schwab - excludes: not found in the evidence provided. No Schwab advisor count or its exclusions was found.
Merrill - excludes: not found in the evidence provided. The only count in the evidence is the GWIM total, whose footnote lists inclusions, not exclusions.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America GWIM supplement and 10-K footnotes

gaps.what: Merrill does not report standalone results.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America GWIM supplement (Total wealth advisors line) for the combined Merrill and Private Bank segment; Merrill-only advisor counts would need a firm statement

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley - reporting: no 2025-2026 period-end advisor count was found in the evidence provided; the only count is for December 2020. No advisor attrition rate was found.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley quarterly financial supplement (Wealth Management metrics page) and earnings calls

gaps.what: Schwab - reporting: no financial consultant or wealth advisor count, and no advisor attrition rate, was found in the evidence provided. Only firm counts for RIA clients and total employee FTEs are disclosed.

Raymond James - attrition: no advisor attrition rate was found in the evidence provided. Management describes retention qualitatively ('high retention', 'departures and planned retirements'). Edward Jones is the only firm in the evidence with a stated attrition rate (6.1% for 3Q25), and its definition is firm-specific.
gaps.suggested_source: Raymond James quarterly earnings supplement or 10-K human capital section
